items.title: Jackie Williams interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995
items.q: The interviewee discusses Dizzy Gillespie's interaction with the Mayor ('Mayor of Syracuse came up and proclaimed “Dizzy Gillespie Day”... Dizzy... went “no shit.”'), but the interviewee (Jackie Williams) does not claim a personal relationship with the Mayor, only narrating an event involving Dizzy

ctx.x: He’s so funny. We had such a good time.

I have to just relate a story of my own quickly. He was playing a jazz festival in Syracuse. And the Mayor of Syracuse came up and proclaimed “Dizzy Gillespie Day” and Dizzy must have been in one of those moods, because he came up to the microphone and he just went “no shit.” You know and there was all these people. And I don’t know I think Mayor went just— He goes “I’m overwhelmed.” And that voice he had made it so much better.

The voice — it would just crack you up you know. He was so funny. God that man was funny. He didn’t even have to open his mouth sometimes. He’d just walk on the stage and you’d start laughing. He’d make those gestures. But he was a natural performer and entertainer also. Heart big as gold. Yeah he was beautiful. Well Judge was so, as he always is, so gracious at this thing, and he said, “Jackie I want you to do whatever you want to do, just fill in and do this.” And I said, “Well whatever you guys want to do you…
